title: Generics and Traits (Part 1) - Reusable behavior
learning_objectives: Write a generic function that works with multiple concrete types.
Define a trait to describe behavior shared by different types.
Use a trait bound to require behavior from a generic parameter.
Explain how generic code preserves compile-time type checking.
explanation: Generics let functions and types work with more than one concrete type without duplicating logic. Traits describe behavior that types can implement, and trait bounds state which behavior generic code needs. The compiler checks each concrete use, so this flexibility does not require sacrificing type safety.

examples.title: Use a generic parameter
Describe shared behavior with a trait
Require an ordering operation
